entity-departing-exitscene-entity-transitions0 of 0.75 (major)failThe requirement says that when an entity exists in one step but not in the step the presentation moves to, it animates out on that transition. The delivered sample does not meet this for most of its departures. SampleScene wraps every entity in Appear, and Appear is the only direct child of the sample&#39;s AnimatePresence (SampleScene.tsx:139-145). When Appear has entering=false, its exit reuses transition={ duration: 0 } (Appear.tsx:26-29), so its opacity drops to 0 instantly. That hides the whole wrapped entity and nothing is animated out. The sample does produce this case. All nine steps share one group and one scene (steps.ts:25-35), and Stage keys the scene by group and component (Stage.tsx:57-66), so the same SampleScene instance stays mounted. Entities only accumulate going forward (steps.ts:6-17; state.ts:60-84), so departures happen only when the user moves backward. SampleScene marks an entity as entering only if it was absent from the previous render (SampleScene.tsx:129-141). Take Left from step 9 to 8 and then from 8 to 7: at step 8, modify-arc, modify-label and flag are rendered with entering=false, because they were already shown at step 9. On 8→7 they leave through the zero-duration exit and vanish without animating. The same happens when a table-of-contents entry jumps backward from step 9: everything except the most recently added entity is continuing and vanishes at once. Judge A gave the fail verdict, and its reason holds up against the source: continuing wrappers are retained by AnimatePresence but exit with duration 0. I rule fail. Judge B (pass) noticed this same caveat but passed anyway on the opt-in-wrapper guidance. That guidance credits a mechanism that keeps a departing entity rendered *while it animates out*. Appear&#39;s continuing path does not animate out, and the sample&#39;s departures go through that path. Judge C (pass) relied on entityProps exit { opacity: 0 } (shared.ts:34-35) and on tests/unit/exit.test.tsx. Neither decides the requirement. skill-scaffold-style-neutralskill-scaffolding0.125 of 0.125 (minor)passThe scaffold&#39;s manifest, build config, host stylesheet and scene kit add no styling framework and set no default visual styling. The only colors, fonts, borders and tokens in the bootstrap are in the bundled sample presentation&#39;s own CSS, which is lazy-loaded with its route and is not applied to other presentations. Dependencies: the bootstrap package.json lists react, react-dom, motion, lucide-react, vite, @vitejs/plugin-react, typescript, ESLint packages and playwright, with no Tailwind, no @tailwindcss/vite and no other CSS framework. vite.config.ts has only the react() plugin, so the app builds without a styling framework. Host stylesheet: src/index.css sets only height:100% and margin:0 on html, body and #root, and its own comment says it sets no visual defaults. Kit styles: presentation-kit/layout.ts holds the kit&#39;s style objects, and every value is positioning or flex geometry (position, display, flex, inset, overflow, alignItems, justifyContent, listStyle none, margin 0, padding 0, and attribution right/bottom offsets). Its header comment says it chooses no color, font, border or spacing scale. Stage.tsx sets only absolute position, size and a scale transform. Toc.tsx sets only listStyle none and zero margin/padding. Footer.tsx, Header.tsx, Attribution.tsx, Arrow.tsx, Box.tsx and SymbolChip.tsx use the layout objects or place() for geometry. Arrow.tsx sets no stroke or fill and exposes data-presentation-arrow-line and data-presentation-arrowhead hooks instead. A grep of bootstrap src (excluding presentations/) for color, font, border, shadow, background, radius and hex/rgb values found only zero margin/padding resets and className/style pass-through props. Landing.tsx renders plain main/h1/ul/li/a with no style or className, and main.tsx and Router.tsx apply no styling. The kit sets no inline visual values. The kit sources have no .css files or CSS imports. The generic kit sits in src/presentation-kit. The registry (src/presentations/index.ts) and Router.tsx/Landing.tsx stay presentation-agnostic. The public title contract is consumed: Talk passes title to Presentation, which forwards it to Header, and Header renders it as data-presentation-deck-title in browse mode. That claim does not answer the majority&#39;s reason, and the cited material shows that reason holds. 1. **Continuing entities exit instantly.** In Appear.tsx the exit is `{ opacity: 0 }` with no transition of its own, so it uses the component&#39;s `transition` prop. The wrapper is therefore kept mounted, but its opacity drops to 0 at once, and the whole wrapped entity disappears without animating. 2. **The sample takes that path.** All nine steps share `groupKey: &#39;sample&#39;` and `SampleScene` (steps.ts), and Stage keys the scene by group and component, so one SampleScene instance stays mounted. Entities only accumulate (ADDITIONS/STATES in steps.ts; visibleEntities in state.ts), so entities leave only when the user moves backward. SampleScene sets `entering` only for ids missing from the previously shown set. Going from step 9 back to 8 renders modify-arc, modify-label and flag with `entering=false`. On the next move, 8→7, those entities exist in step 8 but not in step 7, and they leave through the zero-duration exit, so they vanish instead of animating out. 3. **The primitive&#39;s exit does not change this.** The Box/Arrow `entityProps` exit of `{ opacity: 0 }` over LAYOUT_T (0.6 s) runs inside an Appear wrapper that has already reached opacity 0, so it is not visible. 4. **The test does not cover this path.** tests/unit/exit.test.tsx renders Box directly under AnimatePresence (and Stage-level group changes). It never exercises Appear with `entering=false`. The review guidance credits an exit mechanism that keeps a departing entity rendered *while it animates out*. SKILL.md also tells the author to keep styling out of the kit and to put it in presentation-owned or host-owned files. The scanning tests and the parity test cover them, and layout.ts, which defines all kit style objects, is present. It asserts on the exit code and output after the child process closes (lines 19-23, 46-59, 165-206). The only setTimeout strings in it (lines 110 and 153) are fault-injection source text written into the copied sample. The test never calls them. tests/integration/inspect.test.ts (lines 1-202) writes fixtures, runs the inspect helper to completion for each variant (lines 120-122), and then asserts on captured output and PNG files. tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts (lines 1-118) materializes the bootstrap and runs npm ci, the build and verify as child processes, asserting only after each one exits. tests/integration/support.ts run() (lines 17-35) resolves on the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event. Its setTimeout is only a SIGKILL timeout guard, not a wait before an assertion. isClosed (lines 92-99) is a single fetch with a timeout. The jsdom unit tests poll instead of sleeping: exit.test.tsx uses `waitFor(..., {timeout: 4000})` (lines 54, 61, 77), and router.test.tsx uses `findByText` (lines 39, 45, 48). Its 30 ms setTimeout (line 17) is a fake lazy loader under test, not a wait before an assertion. A search of tests/ found no waitForTimeout or sleep calls. Judges A and B said pass, and the material bears out their reason. Judge C&#39;s reason does not decide the requirement. The page.waitForTimeout calls it cites are in scripts/verify.mjs (lines 114, 143) and scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs. Those are the delivered verification and inspection scripts, not the automated tests this criterion judges. Even inside verify.mjs, the step change is awaited by polling `waitForFunction` on `data-step-index` (lines 129-135). SETTLE_MS is a window for collecting late errors. The inspect.test.ts check that captures come at least the settle interval after each step change (lines 145-149) asserts on the helper&#39;s output after it exits. The kit and its bootstrap-template copy are updated together."},{"line":2950,"text":"- **Regression coverage:** `tests/unit/stage.test.tsx`, \"fits the stage width, not the window width, when a side column narrows the stage\". I did not add it because the instructions for this step bar running that suite, and an unrun test would be unverified. No further change."},{"line":2980,"text":"- **F-002 (scene text about one-third of its CSS size at 390 px):** Still reproduces, and remains an open decision for the user (options 1–4 in the round-0 F-002 section; my recommendation is still option 2). The measured scale of 0.334 is lower than the kit's own width limit of (390 − 48) / 880 = 0.389, because the sample's root padding of 24 px per side narrowed the stage further. I fixed that part: at widths up to 640 px the sample's root padding is now 8 px per side, so the width-limited scale rises to about 0.37 (an increase of roughly 10 %). That is the most that can be gained without changing the sample's composition or the fixed-canvas contract. It does not make 11–13 px design text legible, so the finding stays open until the user picks an option. Those interactive agent steps could not be truthfully exercised by this acceptance agent without a separate agent session and user transcript; no such runner surface was available under this workflow."},{"line":2469,"text":"2. **Public skill modify/coexistence (AT-002): not exercised dynamically.** The instructions were inspected, but no second agent-generated presentation was created and no ambiguous modification request was enacted. The presentation host’s typed payload boundary, exact group instance identity, transient morph ordering, departing-entity animation timing, and raw-motion author extension were not directly observable in this pass. TOC jump to “the loop” reached index 7. Progress jump reached index 8; ArrowRight at the end remained at 8; progress jump to index 0 then ArrowLeft remained at 0. A focused mode-toggle button kept ArrowRight from advancing. Toggling to present at index 7 preserved the index and hid caption, TOC and prev/next controls; active title/marker remained visible. Synthetic horizontal touch events advanced from index 0 to 1. A physical touchscreen and vertical/small swipes were not exercised."},{"line":2472,"text":"5. **Visual/fixed-canvas sample:** project-local helper captured all nine steps at 1440×900 and all nine at 390×900. AXI confirmed attribution text and href `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`. The DOM canvas CSS remained 880×380 and uniformly scaled."},{"line":2473,"text":"6. **Verification success/failure contract and repair loop (AT-004): limited.** A scratch project build passed; production `npm run verify` and the E2E failure cases were not run because acceptance rules prohibit running automated suites. The project-local screenshot helper was exercised on the real sample; it captured settled screenshots and reported the outputs above. Controlled overlap/allow-overlap, indistinct active-state, and unpolished-attribution fixtures were not injected, so the helper’s advisory branches and the skill’s fix-and-rerun behavior remain unverified."},{"line":2474,"text":"7. **Canonical sample verification:** route rendered at `http://127.0.0.1:5173/how-to-make-a-presentation`; AXI snapshot showed 1/9, 2/9, 8/9, and the nine labeled step buttons; helper traversed indices 0–8 without errors. `npm run verify` was deliberately not run, so its exact nine-title/caption assertions, IPv4 internal readiness probe, console/transition failure attribution, exit code, and subprocess cleanup are not acceptance evidence."},{"line":2475,"text":"8. **Template/style ownership:** standalone scaffold build passed without a styling framework. Existing host scripts remain intact. A generated app should build."},{"line":2484,"text":"- **Observation:** The helper reported `relation=presentations`, signals `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `apps/`, `needsConfirmation=true`, anchors `{build:true,kit:false,index:false}`, and missing anchors `[kit,index]`. That command still invokes the host script, which could produce an unrelated success result."},{"line":1035,"text":"- **Options:** Preserve the host script and direct the agent to a namespaced verification command; wrap or rename the host script after explicit confirmation; or keep the existing value and require a functional scene-verification check before reporting success."},{"line":1036,"text":"- **Consequence:** Leaving the conflict unresolved can make skill self-verification report success without building or rendering the presentation. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified goes to \"the and-scene GitHub repository\" but gives no URL."},{"line":841,"text":"- Ruling: The link is `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`, the repository's `origin` remote. It reads exactly \"made by and-scene\", opens as a normal anchor, and carries a stable `data-presentation-attribution` hook."},{"line":842,"text":"- Rationale: The remote is the only repository identity in the workspace. A hook name under the `data-presentation-*` convention is required by the spec and by CLAUDE.md."},{"line":843,"text":"- Pending decision: None."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-54292d93f1a7eb60 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":863,"end_line":873,"lines":[{"line":863,"text":"## What counts as a horizontal swipe?"},{"line":864,"text":"- Requirement: Touch swipe. Left advances, right goes back. No threshold is given."},{"line":865,"text":"- Ruling: A swipe needs at least 50 px of horizontal travel and more horizontal than vertical travel. Anything else is ignored, so vertical scrolling does not navigate."},{"line":866,"text":"- Rationale: A threshold is needed to be deterministic and unit-testable. 50 px is a common default."},{"line":867,"text":"- Pending decision: None."},{"line":868,"text":""},{"line":869,"text":"## At what width does the table of contents show?"},{"line":870,"text":"- Requirement: Browse mode shows the table of contents \"on wide viewports\". No breakpoint is given."},{"line":871,"text":"- Ruling: The table of contents renders only in browse mode at viewport widths of 1024 px or more. It is a single named constant in the kit. The \"standard desktop viewport\" for screenshots is 1440×900, and the narrow viewport is 390 px wide."},{"line":872,"text":"- Rationale: 1024 px is a conventional desktop breakpoint, and the 1440 px desktop viewport is above it."},{"line":873,"text":"- Pending decision: None."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-54292d93f1a7eb60 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1025,"end_line":1029,"lines":[{"line":1025,"text":"## May `npm test` include a fast test that runs the scaffold CLI in a child process? (audit at HEAD 04335b0b)"},{"line":1026,"text":"- Requirement: CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md implementation workflow: \"Keep `npm test` to fast unit and contract tests. Put slower integration, end-to-end, and browser-backed tests in a separate npm script.\" Test plan, \"Coverage Strategy\": the integration layer targets risks that \"require real filesystem materialization, subprocesses, a production browser, or an agent following the public skill workflow\", and INT-001 covers template lookup independent of the caller's working directory. Code read: `tests/unit/scaffold.test.ts` lines 377–384 (\"runs from an unrelated cwd and prints JSON\", using `execFileAsync(process.execPath, [SCRIPT, project], { cwd: elsewhere })`), `package.json` scripts (`test`, `test:integration`, `test:e2e`)."},{"line":1027,"text":"- Ruling: Permitted, and not a finding. My earlier section \"How are the npm test scripts split?\" said `npm test` has \"no browser or subprocess\". That was stricter than the approved definition and I withdraw the subprocess half. The approved rule for `npm test` is about kind and speed: fast unit and contract tests, with slower integration, end-to-end and browser-backed tests in separate scripts. It does not ban a child process. A single short Node process that runs the dependency-free repository script on a temporary directory, with no browser, no dependency install, no build, no network and no server, is a fast contract test of the CLI's output (JSON shape, target, missing anchors). Its logged run of 42 ms is consistent with that. PS \"Self-verify\" (responsive-sensitive presentations are checked at a narrow viewport)."},{"line":1050,"text":"- **Analysis:** The scale at 390 px is (390 − 48) / 880, about 0.39, and that follows directly from the approved model. The measured scale of 0.334 is lower than the kit's own width limit of (390 − 48) / 880 = 0.389, because the sample's root padding of 24 px per side narrowed the stage further. I fixed that part: at widths up to 640 px the sample's root padding is now 8 px per side, so the width-limited scale rises to about 0.37 (an increase of roughly 10 %). That is the most that can be gained without changing the sample's composition or the fixed-canvas contract. It does not make 11–13 px design text legible, so the finding stays open until the user picks an option. I did not redesign the sample's type and chip geometry on my own, because I cannot check collisions in a browser in this step and the choice among the options is not mine. Unit result: `evidence/acceptance-fix-round1-unit.log` (kit and template parity, sample and unstyled-kit contracts; 31 passed). The CSS change itself is not covered by a unit test and needs the next round's measurement."},{"line":1074,"text":"- **I-001:** Resolved. The tester's final refresh shows `mergeable=MERGEABLE` and `mergeStateStatus=CLEAN`, and the pull request head matches the tested revision. The transient `UNKNOWN` state was GitHub recomputing mergeability after the merge of `main`. My own query of the pull request after that returned the same CLEAN state."},{"line":1075,"text":"- **I-002:** Unchanged and not fixable from this repository. A newer `gh`, or a plugin build that omits `baseRefOid`, is needed. The repository has no hosted CI, so no check is waiting. A direct `gh pr checks` query worked."},{"line":1076,"text":"- **Pending decision:** Which F-002 option to adopt; whether to upgrade `gh` or the plugin."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-54292d93f1a7eb60 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1226,"end_line":1230,"lines":[{"line":1226,"text":"1. **Public skill gathering, scaffolding and creation (AT-001): partially exercised.** Read the complete public skill. Self-verify before reporting completion"},{"line":1493,"text":""},{"line":1494,"text":"Do not report success until every check below passes. When a check fails, fix the cause in the presentation or the host, then re-run that check and the checks after it."},{"line":1495,"text":""},{"line":1496,"text":"1. Build: run `npm run build` in `target.appDir`. It must finish with no type errors."},{"line":1497,"text":"2. Project checks: run `npm run verify` in `target.appDir`. It builds the app, checks the registry and the bundled sample, and renders and steps through the sample in a browser. It prints `PASS`, or `FAIL <phase>` with a step index for render and transition failures. Any failure must be fixed and re-run."},{"line":1498,"text":"3. Visual composition: run `npm run inspect -- <slug>`. It writes settled screenshots to `.inspection/<slug>/step-NN.png` (two digits, starting at 1). Any console or page error reported for the first step counts as a failure of the first-step render check."},{"line":1499,"text":"4. View the screenshots of the first step, the last step, and every dense or key step. Check that the content fits the fixed canvas, that intentional overlaps stay readable, and that no content collides with captions, the progress indicator, the table of contents, or the navigation controls."},{"line":1500,"text":"5. Responsive check: if the presentation is responsive-sensitive (wrapping text, many entities, or dense steps), also inspect at a narrow viewport of 390 px wide, using the helper's narrow-viewport option shown in `npm run inspect -- --help`."},{"line":1501,"text":"6. Review advisory warnings: the inspection output lists overlap and chrome-polish warnings by step. Warnings do not fail the run, but you must review every warning that cites a step. Then:"},{"line":1502,"text":" - Fix accidental collisions by moving, resizing, or reflowing the content."},{"line":1503,"text":" - Fix active chrome that is not visibly distinct from the inactive chrome, and attribution that is too small or still browser-default, by changing the presentation's CSS."},{"line":1504,"text":" - Mark an overlap only when it is intentional and readable, by adding the attribute `data-presentation-allow-overlap` to the element that contains the overlap."},{"line":1505,"text":" - Re-run `npm run build`, `npm run verify`, and `npm run inspect -- <slug>` after any change."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-f215b1d33f8bec15 (referenced-material)]"}],"assumption-decisions-and-escalations-proportionate":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":40,"end_line":40,"lines":[{"line":40,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Interactive requirement gathering\\nThe skill SHALL gather presentation details by asking the user clarifying questions one at a time — covering the topic, the visual style, and the content and visual description of each step. The user controls how much to specify; the skill SHALL NOT assume details the user can still provide, but SHALL allow the user to proceed with partial detail and iterate. The skill MAY, at its discretion, draw ASCII mockups to represent key or complex steps when doing so helps confirm the intended visual layout.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt is missing details\\n- **WHEN** the skill is invoked with a prompt that omits the topic, visual style, or per-step descriptions\\n- **THEN** the skill asks for the missing information one question at a time rather than assuming it\\n\\n#### Scenario: User proceeds with partial detail\\n- **WHEN** the user chooses to build after providing only some details\\n- **THEN** the skill generates a presentation from what was captured without blocking on a hard completeness gate\\n\\n#### Scenario: Prompt already complete\\n- **WHEN** the prompt already contains the topic, style, and all step details\\n- **THEN** the skill may proceed to build without further questions\\n\\n#### Scenario: ASCII mockup for a complex step\\n- **WHEN** a step's visual layout is key or complex\\n- **THEN** the skill may present an ASCII mockup of that step to the user to confirm the layout before building, without doing so for every step\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-bootstrapping scaffold\\nBefore creating or modifying a presentation, the skill SHALL ensure the project provides the infrastructure a generated presentation depends on, SHALL resolve where that infrastructure belongs, and SHALL scaffold whatever is missing — including installing the dependencies the infrastructure requires. The required infrastructure is three contract anchors:\\n\\n1. **Build setup** — a Vite + React + TypeScript app with a working `npm run build`.\\n2. **Scene kit** — the reusable, presentation-agnostic engine: the `Step`/`Scene` step contract, the stage/host that mounts the active step and runs entity morphs, the present/browse navigation, and the chrome (captions, table of contents) and fit-scale canvas.\\n3. **Presentation index** — the registry that maps each presentation to its own route so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\nDetection is contract-level, keyed on the presence of these anchors rather than a byte-identical scaffold, so cosmetic differences (file naming, formatting, extra dependencies) do not trigger re-scaffolding. When scaffolding, the skill SHALL NOT assume the required dependencies are already installed.\\n\\nThe scaffold SHALL be styling-framework-neutral and SHALL ship with zero presentation styling defaults. It SHALL install the runtime and build dependencies needed for React, Vite, TypeScript, Motion, Lucide icons, linting, and render verification, but it SHALL NOT require Tailwind, a Tailwind Vite plugin, a default CSS theme, default colors, default fonts, default card styles, default button styles, or any other styling framework. Styling systems MAY be added by the presentation author or host project after scaffolding.\\n\\nThe skill SHALL resolve scaffold templates relative to the skill file that declares them, so agents do not depend on the user's current working directory when locating `templates/bootstrap/` or presentation templates.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Empty or fully unscaffolded directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs in an empty directory or a project with none of the three anchors present\\n- **THEN** it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, and presentation index) and installs the required dependencies before creating the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Already scaffolded\\n- **WHEN** all three anchors are already present\\n- **THEN** the skill skips scaffolding and proceeds directly to creating or modifying the presentation\\n\\n#### Scenario: Partial scaffold\\n- **WHEN** some but not all anchors are present\\n- **THEN** the skill scaffolds only the missing anchors (and their dependencies) without disturbing the ones already present\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scaffold does not impose a style system\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds a presentation app\\n- **THEN** the generated app can build without Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **AND** the scaffold does not define default presentation colors, fonts, spacing scale, card styles, button styles, borders, shadows, or CSS theme tokens\\n\\n#### Scenario: Templates resolve from skill directory\\n- **WHEN** the skill copies bootstrap or presentation templates\\n- **THEN** it resolves those paths relative to the skill's own `SKILL.md` directory\\n\\n#### Scenario: Monorepo target\\n- **WHEN** the skill runs inside a monorepo\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app into a `presentations/` directory as its own self-contained app rather than at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Standalone project target\\n- **WHEN** the skill scaffolds in an empty or standalone (non-monorepo) project\\n- **THEN** it scaffolds the presentation app at the repository root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Non-empty project missing scaffolding\\n- **WHEN** the project is non-empty but lacks the scene kit or presentation index\\n- **THEN** the skill states the target location it will scaffold into and proceeds only after the user confirms\\n\\n### Requirement: Create a new presentation\\nThe skill SHALL generate a new presentation as a self-contained unit reachable at its own route and registered so that multiple presentations coexist.\\n\\n#### Scenario: New presentation is self-contained and routed\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created\\n- **THEN** it is written as its own folder, reachable at its own route, and registered in the presentation index\\n\\n#### Scenario: Presentation owns its visual style\\n- **WHEN** the skill creates a presentation with a designed visual look\\n- **THEN** the styling is added in files owned by that presentation or by the host app rather than in the reusable scene kit\\n- **AND** plain CSS is the default styling approach unless the host project already uses a styling framework or the user explicitly requests one\\n\\n#### Scenario: Existing presentations are preserved\\n- **WHEN** a new presentation is created and other presentations already exist\\n- **THEN** the existing presentations remain intact and reachable\\n\\n### Requirement: Modify an existing presentation\\nThe skill SHALL support modifying an existing presentation, identifying the target first and asking only about the requested changes.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Target unspecified or ambiguous\\n- **WHEN** the skill is asked to modify a presentation without a clear target\\n- **THEN** it lists the existing presentations and asks which to modify before changing anything\\n\\n#### Scenario: Scoped modification\\n- **WHEN** the target presentation is identified\\n- **THEN** the skill asks only about the requested changes (steps, entities, or style) and edits that presentation without re-walking the full create flow\\n\\n### Requirement: Self-verify before reporting completion\\nBefore reporting success, the skill SHALL confirm that the generated or modified presentation builds, renders without errors, and is visually coherent in a browser, fixing any failures itself. The render check SHALL at minimum render the presentation's first step without runtime or console errors; the full multi-step render check across every step is defined by the `presentation-verification` capability. The visual composition check SHALL inspect screenshots or an equivalent browser view of the first step, the last step, and any dense/key steps; responsive-sensitive presentations SHALL also be checked at a narrow viewport. When a project-local screenshot helper is available, the skill SHALL prefer it over ad hoc scripts outside the project tree so browser tooling resolves from local dependencies, settled screenshots are captured after animations complete, and advisory visual warnings can be reviewed.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Checks run before done\\n- **WHEN** the skill finishes generating or modifying a presentation\\n- **THEN** it runs the build, at least a first-step render check, and a browser visual composition check before reporting completion\\n\\n#### Scenario: Failures are fixed, not reported as success\\n- **WHEN** the build, render, or visual composition check fails\\n- **THEN** the skill fixes the issues and re-checks rather than reporting success\\n\\n### Requirement: Generated presentation quality bar\\nEvery generated presentation SHALL build with no type errors, render its first step without runtime errors, present a caption per step, support next/previous navigation, pass a visual composition check, and conform to the evolving-scene model.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Builds clean\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated\\n- **THEN** `npm run build` completes with no type errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Renders without errors\\n- **WHEN** the presentation route is opened\\n- **THEN** it renders its first step with no runtime or console errors\\n\\n#### Scenario: Captions and navigation present\\n- **WHEN** viewing a presentation\\n- **THEN** each step shows a caption and the user can navigate to the next and previous steps\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual composition is inspected\\n- **WHEN** a presentation is generated or modified\\n- **THEN** key browser screenshots or equivalent browser views show that important scene content fits the fixed canvas, intentional overlaps remain readable, and content does not collide with chrome such as captions, progress indicators, table of contents, or navigation controls\\n\\n#### Scenario: Screenshot helper is project-local\\n- **WHEN** the skill captures screenshots for visual inspection\\n- **THEN** it uses the scaffolded project-local helper when available, or otherwise writes any temporary Playwright helper under the project root\\n\\n#### Scenario: Visual warnings are reviewed\\n- **WHEN** the screenshot helper emits overlap or chrome-polish warnings\\n- **THEN** the skill reviews the referenced steps, fixes accidental collisions or indistinct current-step chrome, and marks only intentional readable overlaps as allowed\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active chrome and attribution are styled locally\\n- **WHEN** the generated presentation includes table-of-contents, progress, navigation, or attribution chrome\\n- **THEN** presentation-owned or host-owned CSS makes the active step visibly distinct and the attribution legible\\n- **AND** the reusable scene kit remains free of default colors, fonts, borders, button styles, and theme tokens\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1031,"end_line":1037,"lines":[{"line":1031,"text":"## How should an existing host `verify` script interact with scaffold Self-verify before reporting completion"},{"line":1493,"text":""},{"line":1494,"text":"Do not report success until every check below passes. When a check fails, fix the cause in the presentation or the host, then re-run that check and the checks after it."},{"line":1495,"text":""},{"line":1496,"text":"1. Build: run `npm run build` in `target.appDir`. It must finish with no type errors."},{"line":1497,"text":"2. Project checks: run `npm run verify` in `target.appDir`. It builds the app, checks the registry and the bundled sample, and renders and steps through the sample in a browser. It prints `PASS`, or `FAIL <phase>` with a step index for render and transition failures. Any failure must be fixed and re-run."},{"line":1498,"text":"3. Visual composition: run `npm run inspect -- <slug>`. It writes settled screenshots to `.inspection/<slug>/step-NN.png` (two digits, starting at 1). Any console or page error reported for the first step counts as a failure of the first-step render check."},{"line":1499,"text":"4. View the screenshots of the first step, the last step, and every dense or key step. Check that the content fits the fixed canvas, that intentional overlaps stay readable, and that no content collides with captions, the progress indicator, the table of contents, or the navigation controls."},{"line":1500,"text":"5. Responsive check: if the presentation is responsive-sensitive (wrapping text, many entities, or dense steps), also inspect at a narrow viewport of 390 px wide, using the helper's narrow-viewport option shown in `npm run inspect -- --help`."},{"line":1501,"text":"6. Review advisory warnings: the inspection output lists overlap and chrome-polish warnings by step. Warnings do not fail the run, but you must review every warning that cites a step. Then:"},{"line":1502,"text":" - Fix accidental collisions by moving, resizing, or reflowing the content."},{"line":1503,"text":" - Fix active chrome that is not visibly distinct from the inactive chrome, and attribution that is too small or still browser-default, by changing the presentation's CSS."},{"line":1504,"text":" - Mark an overlap only when it is intentional and readable, by adding the attribute `data-presentation-allow-overlap` to the element that contains the overlap."},{"line":1505,"text":" - Re-run `npm run build`, `npm run verify`, and `npm run inspect -- <slug>` after any change."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-f215b1d33f8bec15 (referenced-material)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1132,"end_line":1138,"lines":[{"line":1132,"text":"Assumptions ledger: `acceptance-assumptions.md`. **Three decisions remain unresolved:**"},{"line":1133,"text":""},{"line":1134,"text":"1. **How should an existing host `verify` script interact with scaffold verification?** Options: preserve the host script and use a namespaced scene verifier; wrap or rename after confirmation; or preserve the value and require a functional verification check.
